newsitem.title: MOROCCO: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - Jan 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - Jan 17.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Morocco's weekly economic press. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Casablanca Bourse ends 1996 with growth of 30 percent, with foreign shareholders making substantial gains. But the paper says a good income is not enough -- a mature market needs to respect equity rules. The Bourse's watchdog, Conseil Deontologique des Valeurs Mobiliers, must reinforce its role in 1997 by dispelling uneasiness created by news of merger between Wafabank and Spanish Uniban and protecting interests of small shareholders.

- French hotel group ACCOR might take over Moroccan Dounia PLM group owned by Abdelhadi Alami. The accord will be final once mortgage bank Credit Immobilier et Hotelier and Banque Commerciale du Maroc, creditors of Dounia PLM, grant concessions demanded by ACCOR. The French group said late last year that a fund of $100 million would be constituted, with the group holding 15 percent and the remainder by foreign investors, to promote tourism in Morocco.

- Interior ministry issues circular urging generalisation of use of bills by production firms and wholesale trade so that there is convergence over ways and means to store goods. The note is in line with an agreement signed between the government and the General Confederation of Moroccan Businesses (CGEM) last April following the crackdown on smuggling.

- Morocco upgrades laws in order to set up a framework favourable for business. After legislation on limited companies it plans to meet the requirements of the World Trade Organisation on agriculture by replacing reference prices by tariff equivalents.
- With decision to set up trade courts, Moroocco's judiciary system takes step towards reform.

- Government ponders law to liberalise prices of domestic pharmaceutical products. Story refers to plans to alleviate red tape hampering the industry. Businessmen propose setting up a reference index allowing them to adjust prices taking account of economic factors, particularly inflation.
